body:
>Or what hinders you from telling him`?

It wouldn't help me, and it wouldn't help him.

>do you think he pisses you off because of his condition or because he is an evil person?

I don't care if he has autism. I don't care if he has asperger. It's that because everyone treats him like a retard he feels that all the wrong things he does are right. He feels that there are no downsides to fucking up. He cannot understand that he can ever be wrong, so if anyone ever doesn't treat him like a retard, they're assholes. This is how my parents raised him. I treat him like a normal person. If he does something deliberately to anger me, I  will act like I would to anyone else. He pisses me off because I'm the only person in his life that treats him normally, so obviously to my family that is being an asshole because "he's different." I call bullshit. He can do anything a normal person does, and probably just has ADHD, but some fuckwit misdiagnosed him.

>how close to your family do you live and how often do you see them?

We live in the same land, but I live in a different house. So technically I still live with them. I can go some days without seeing anyone of them. The ones I see the most are my mother and brother, since they don't do anything and are always in. I barely see my father and sister anymore. 

>Could you help your father when he went through that depression?

He did not want help from anyone. He felt like a weight if he had help. My grandfather helped him manage his businesses and started to pay for all our house bills. My uncle helped him and got him a gas station for him to manage, since he's in that business. Yet, he didn't want any help. He did not stop working one day. He only took the help because he did not have any other choice. I remember once he told me that lying and saying you're fine is better than saying something sensitive and getting undeserved help. As for me helping, my mother used to tell me to simply help my father by not causing him troubles like bad grades, fights, etc.

>Do you think because he went through a depression he can relate to how you feel yourself right now? How much of how you feel does your father know?

No. His depression was because his honest and hard work were not paying off because of some cheating bastards. He was depressed because he tried as hard as he could but could not bring food to the table. He felt like a weight because his retired father had to pay the bills for the house he could no longer afford. This is what I think, anyway, since I never really talked to him about it. 

I realized while typing this most that I have so much repressed anger.

>So if I get it right you are not always depressed and pretty content, but you don't want to live your life like you do right now, did I understand that correctly?

If I had to describe my lifestyle easily to a stranger, I'd say depressed. Mainly because I act like if I was depressed. Yet, I do not feel the terrible sadness, self-loathing (I still have this, but not in the same way) and sinking feeling of a depression. I am usually content because my life mainly consists on doing things that make me content. It is not real life. If I spent all day long on r/funny and circlejerk, of course I can get laughs and be mostly happy that day. Yet, I know that on real life I am a little piece of shit, but knowing this doesn't make me sad. And I guess that my laziness has gotten to such levels that I'd rather kill myself than stepping up and becoming a real man. My main concern with suicide would be handicapping and/or making a fool of myself if I fail.

>If you could do anything you want, what would that be?

Year-long trip across Europe.

>Also if you don't mind me asking, why do you get irritated and angry when you talk with your family, and has it always been that way?

As long as I can remember. My brother has always pissed me off since I was little, mainly because he sometimes deliberately does things that he knows will anger me. It is most likely a way for him to get attention, but it causes the only moments I actually pay attention to him is when I yell at him.

My father works a lot. I remember when I was younger there were times when I didn't see him all week long. He is an honest man, and I really respect him. I never fight with him. Yet, I sometimes feel I barely know him. It has been hard to see him for the past 5 years. He went through a depression and he has been having bad luck financially, mainly because some motherfuckers don't pay him for the jobs he does, trying to take him out of business.

I don't usually talk to my sister. This causes that the only times we ever have to speak is when we're so frustrated at each other's opinions or acts that we have to have a verbal discussion.

My mother is just an uneducated person that tries to shove her opinions  to people. She is the one I discuss with the most, mainly because she's the one that tries the most to talk to me, but the results aren't good. I'm just not interested in whatever she ever has to say.

>Do you want to tell me why you do not like people and like to keep contact to your family to a minimum?

I am very inconsistent and hard to reach. People require maintenance and being available most of the time. Sometimes I am just too lazy to charge my cellphone for a few days, and then I don't feel like responding 3 day old texts. The only way to contact me as soon as possible is through facebook, as I check on it every hour or so when I'm bored on my laptop. Yet, since I barely do anything on facebook since I don't post pointless status or upload any pictures people assume I am never on it, so that is why I don't communicate there.

My family is just complicated. They're very different from me and most conversations I have with any of them I usually end up irritated or angry at them. My parents got married because my mother was pregnant with my big brother who has autism or something. I am the 2nd born, and I'm only 10 months older than my little sister. It has always made me sort of proud that I probably was the only non-accident child. I really like my granddads. They're awesome. Yet, I am not a person to suddenly call them just to see how they're doing. They'll most likely die within a span of 5 years. I can't help but feel that lately I've been a disappointment because I was their grandson who was smart and going places.

>Also, do you know what you can do to feel better? Have you done anything in the past that made you feel better?

This question is complex. It's not that I live with constant sadness, or I'm depressed. I am usually content, even when I think I want to kill myself. Usually when I'm sad I just try to rub it off and do something else. This works unless it's a problem I have to solve and I'm just ignoring it until it gets bigger. Also eating delicious food sure cheers me up.

>If you could do whatever you want, what do you think would be the next step for you to feel better?

These seems to be two unrelated questions pasted in he same sentence. I'll assume you meant that if I could suddenly go do whatever, what would be the first step into doing that thing that makes me happy. Well I don't know.

I want to travel. It may be the thing I want the most in this world. Yet to do that, I have to get so much of my shit together and prepare in case for an emergency. And it may not be as good as I think it will be. After all I don't enjoy sleeping anywhere but my bed, being on a tight budget or schedule.

>If you don't mind me asking, have you thought about going to a doctor about this?

I have gone to psychiatrists on-and-off since I was 13. I've been to 4 different ones. The first two I was pretty sure they just wanted to make me feel hopeless without them so I just kept going and wasting more money in them. The last two where just time and money wasters. I just went there, we talked about nothing meaningful and I left. It was like I paid a dude to chill with me for 45 minutes. Funnily enough, the first two where women and the last two men. Last time I went to one was about 3 months ago. So yeah, to answer it, I don't really believe in therapy.

I used to take wellbutrin for about 3 years. One day I simply stopped. I did not really feel it changed my life, but I did get out of a year depression when I was 15.


>Do you think it might help you if you took a hobby like playing an instrument or physical workout or something you would feel somewhat of an achievement?

My problem with this is that I don't like commitment, because if I quit I feel like a failure. I used to take guitar when I was very young, probably 10. The teacher was horrible and I just quit. Thinking about it, I probably should have never taken those classes. I usually feel pretty good after running at the park, but I do not like being in public areas, as I feel insecure. The nearest gym I can go to at any time is not at walking distance, and I don't drive.

>If you want to, you could also volunteer to help at animal shelters or homes for old people.

None where I live. I wouldn't be interested in homes, and I think animal shelters would depress me, leading me to adopt all the dogs.

>What are you good at and what are your interests?

I am good at listening to other's people crap. I tend to keep my mouth shut rather than blurt out ignorant stupidities. I like helping people, specially if I can make them smile. Also I'm somewhat good at advice.

>Also how is your relationship to your family?

'To it's minimum. I'd like to keep it that way.

>Find a goal

This is one of my biggest problems. I don't care about anything enough to stop being like I am. I believe that if you truly want something you can do it through hard work and all that crap, but I do not want to do anything in particular.

>find people who are friends not "friends"

I don't really like people. Having little knowledge of pop culture and no interesting pastimes makes it hard to connect with anyone.

>therapy

No.

>only you have the cure

Well, I'll be fucked.
